question: Which statement best describes How declarations are hoisted?
options: Before executing a scope, the engine does a creation phase: it scans for declarations and registers their names in the scope. Conceptually the declarations are 'moved to the top', though nothing literally moves — the bindings are simply created before any line runs. How they are initialized depends on the keyword.

Function declarations are hoisted with their entire body, so they are callable before they appear in the source. Function expressions only hoist the variable binding — `undefined` for var, TDZ for let/const — so calling them early fails. This is the most practical hoisting difference to remember.

A `var` declaration is hoisted and immediately initialized to `undefined`, so you can reference it before its line without an error — you just get `undefined` until the assignment runs. This split between declaration and assignment surprises many developers and is a frequent source of bugs.

`let` and `const` are also hoisted — the engine knows their names — but they are NOT initialized. From the start of the block until the declaration line, the binding is in the temporal dead zone (TDZ), and any access throws a ReferenceError. This makes use-before-declare an explicit error instead of a silent `undefined`.
